references.text: Both verses describe the burnt offering as 'a pleasing aroma to the Lord' (רֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ לַיהוָה), and the priest burns the offering on the altar.
It also describes a bird offering where the bird is not to be completely separated, similar to the instruction not to separate the wings.
The priest burns the offering on the altar as a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma to the Lord - the same concluding formula as in verse 17.
Noah's offering after the flood is described as 'a pleasing aroma' (רֵיחַ הַנִּיחֹחַ) to the Lord, the first occurrence of this expression.
The burnt offering of the ram is described as 'a pleasing aroma, a food offering to the Lord' (רֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ אִשֶּׁה לַיהוָה).
A fire offering to the Lord as a pleasing aroma (רֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ לַיהוָה) - the same terminology for an offering that pleases God.
Paul uses Old Testament sacrifice terminology and describes Christ's offering as 'a fragrant gift and a sacrifice to God' (εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας).
The parallel shows that both animal and vegetable offerings can become a pleasing aroma to the Lord, expanding the understanding of what is accepted as sanctifying.
